status: shadow research; NOT Spotify-published; no actual listening A/B
brief: 12 real, musically coherent recordings moving from hypnotic guitar grooves to unusual vocals, repetition and studio experimentation

comparison.title: The Wrong Turn That Works
comparison.description: From Saigon electric pop through cumbia, Sahel guitar, Turkish grooves, Zamrock and Ghanaian funk to ensemble-vocal intensity and a beautifully stubborn experimental-rock finish.
comparison.route: preserve A's enjoyable arc, substitute only method/role-backed transitions

mirlos.method: repeating guitar line and dance pulse

nusrat.method: chorus/lead response and intensification in a devotional context

magma.track: Da Zeuhl Wortz Mekanïk (1973 album sequence)
magma.method: ensemble vocals and insistent rhythmic development

etran.method: cycling guitar figures and ensemble momentum

ebo.date_context: 1977 original on Ebo Taylor LP; online reissue
role: transition from guitar fuzz to arranged jazz/funk

heat_efficiency.track: Health and Efficiency (1980 studio single; artist remaster)
role: convert Magma's group intensity into a hard-driving, comparatively songlike finale

mechanism.operation: move cycling melodic riffs from Peruvian cumbia toward Saharan ensemble propulsion
mechanism.role: retain a recognizable groove while crossing a large stylistic/geographic distance

changes.benefit: a meaningful long-distance guitar bridge rather than a second guitar-psych reference
changes.risk: a contemporary Niger recording between older Peruvian and Turkish studio sounds can reveal a production-era jump

mechanism.material: electric guitars, live funk rhythm, arranged horns
mechanism.operation: move a heavy fuzz-rock groove toward layered Ghanaian highlife/funk
mechanism.role: keep the listener dancing while preparing Hailu Mergia's instrumental ensemble sound

changes.outgoing: Ebo Taylor → Hailu Mergia & Walias Band
changes.benefit: removes back-to-back Zamrock artists and bridges toward Ethio-jazz via funk arrangement
changes.risk: 'Heaven' is a longer cut; transition depends on actual dynamics, which have not been listened to

mechanism.material: experimental rock group, instrumental momentum and an opening vocal passage
mechanism.operation: replace primarily tape-loop demonstration with a gradually intensifying live-band composition
mechanism.role: resolve Magma's ensemble force in a driving finale without switching to pure sound art

changes.benefit: retains This Heat eccentricity but finishes on an energetic band track, not a tape-loop exercise
changes.risk: still an eight-minute long-form track, not a guaranteed breezy closer

verification: New candidate identities verified on official artist/label release pages; inherited nine retain original A's varying catalog evidence. Exact provider IDs and live availability unknown.
evaluation_plan: Compare A and C in order; mark #3→4→5, #6→7→8 and #11→12 as stronger/same/weaker; rate whole-list listenability and unexpected-but-musical transitions independently. No scores recorded before actual hearing.
limitations: The same curator constructed A and C without blinding or machine-based music evaluation.
A one-to-one source listing does not ensure correct playable track resolution on Spotify.
Benefits and risks are predictions from documented instrumentation/production rather than a personal audio audition.
The method-layer is open-universe reasoning, not a Nurse with Wound artist rank boost.
Existing nine A tracks have prior varying-strength sources; no across-the-board service matching was performed.
